issues.description: The problem statement requires calculateTotalPrice(Meal) to be a static method (shared across all SealSaloon instances), but the solution implements it as an instance method (non-static). This contradicts the specification and can confuse students about whether calculateTotalPrice should be static or instance-level and how to call it.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the implementation with the specification: declare calculateTotalPrice as static in SealSaloon (public static int calculateTotalPrice(Meal meal)) and update any calls/tests to reference it appropriately, or alternatively update the problem statement to remove the requirement that calculateTotalPrice be static so an instance method is allowed. Ensure the template and solution use the same static/instance convention.

issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to initialize the SealSaloon attributes (orders and stock) in the constructor, but it also requires the stock attribute to be static. Initializing a static stock in the instance constructor (as the instructions suggest) is inconsistent and will confuse students about where/how to initialize the shared stock.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the intended design: either (A) make stock an instance final field and keep the instruction to initialize it in the constructor, or (B) keep stock static and update the constructor instructions to only initialize instance fields (orders), and show that stock should be initialized statically (e.g., private static final Stock stock = new Stock();). Update the problem text and template accordingly so students are not asked to initialize a static field in the instance constructor.
